steps.message:
We're finally retiring the old Perl request signer. The TypeScript replacement in
`/app/src/pipeline.ts` was started by someone who has since left the team, and it
doesn't work. It compiles fine and it writes evidence, but the gateway rejects
every signature it produces.

They wrote it from `/app/dossier/01-decision-register.md`. The rest of
`/app/dossier/` is everything else the migration left behind: the notes from
each session between kickoff and rollout, and the appendices. The scheme went
live at the 2025-12-09 rollout, and what the gateway checks is the scheme as it
stood on that day.

Finish the port.

## What it has to do

Read a JSON array of request records on stdin, handle each one in order, and
write newline delimited evidence JSON to stdout. One compact object per line,
every line ending in LF including the last one.

Each record gets signed or verified under GW-HMAC-SHA256. If a record carries an
`Authorization` header, verify it. If it doesn't, sign it.

Every evidence object has exactly these keys, in this order:

- `seq`, the 1-based position of the record in the input
- `key_id`, the key id from the request, or `""` when there isn't one
- `method`, the HTTP method uppercased
- `path`, the request target up to but not including the first `?`
- `outcome`, one of `signed`, `verified`, or `rejected`
- `signature`, the lowercase hex HMAC of the record's canonical request. It is
  filled whenever the record names a key on the active roster, even if the record
  is then rejected, and is `""` only for `missing-key-id` and `unknown-key-id`
- `canonical_sha256`, lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical request string
- `reason`, present only when `outcome` is `rejected`

The 4 rejection reasons are `missing-key-id`, `unknown-key-id`,
`malformed-authorization`, and `signature-mismatch`, checked in that order. An
`Authorization` header is well formed when it starts with exactly
`GW-HMAC-SHA256 keyId=<the record's key id>, signature=`, and anything else is
`malformed-authorization`. Whatever follows `signature=` is the presented
signature, compared as is apart from surrounding whitespace, so a well formed
header carrying a wrong, short or non-hex signature is a `signature-mismatch`.

## Keys

Keys are in `/app/keys`. Not every file in there is on the active roster.
`/app/captures/` has traces pulled off the signers running on the production
host. The strace and the lsof of the legacy request signer settle between them
which keys it actually used and how it read them. A request naming a key that
isn't on the roster is an `unknown-key-id`, never signed.

Those 2 captures also show that request signing is pure local computation. The
replacement must not touch the network, and must not reference any network
client in its sources.

## Build and run

CI drives this, so keep the entry points where they are. Sources stay under
`/app/src`, the build stays `tsc -p /app/tsconfig.json` producing
`/app/dist/pipeline.js`, and it runs as:

```
node /app/dist/pipeline.js < <requests.json> > <evidence.ndjson>
```

Same input, same bytes, every time. CI points it at request sets other than the
one shipped here, so don't special case anything to the sample.

## What to leave behind

Run it over `/app/requests/sample-requests.json` and put the result in
`/app/out/evidence.ndjson`.

arguments.command: cd /app; ls -R . | grep -v node_modules | head -80; cat src/pipeline.ts; cat tsconfig.json; wc -c dossier/*

raw_arguments.command: cd /app; ls -R . | grep -v node_modules | head -80; cat src/pipeline.ts; cat tsconfig.json; wc -c dossier/*

arguments.command: cd /app; cat dossier/01-decision-register.md captures/README.md; cat captures/*.lsof; cat captures/*.strace | head -150; ls -la keys; head -c 300 requests/*; for f in keys/*; do xxd $f | head -5; done

raw_arguments.command: cd /app; cat dossier/01-decision-register.md captures/README.md; cat captures/*.lsof; cat captures/*.strace | head -150; ls -la keys; head -c 300 requests/*; for f in keys/*; do xxd $f | head -5; done

# Gateway Signing Migration - Decision Register

Status: living document. Entries are appended in decision order and are
NEVER edited in place. Where a later meeting reverses an entry, the
reversal is recorded in that meeting's note and the entry below is left
standing as the historical record.

## GW-002

The signing scheme identifier is the literal string `GW-HMAC-SHA256`. It appears in the Authorization header and nowhere in the canonical request.

_Recorded by S. Varga (identity)._

## GW-004

Signatures are HMAC-SHA256, rendered as LOWERCASE hexadecimal. Base64 was considered and rejected: too many partners mangled the padding.

_Recorded by A. Nakamura (identity)._

## GW-009

Requests with an empty or absent body sign the literal token `UNSIGNED` in the body-hash field, matching the behaviour of the 2019 signer.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (fraud-ops)._

## GW-011

The canonical request has exactly 6 fields, joined by LF, in this order: HTTP method (uppercased); path; canonical query; canonical header block; signed header name list; body hash.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (billing)._

## GW-013

The path is the request target up to but not including the first `?`. It is signed as received, without normalisation: no dot-segment collapsing, no re-encoding.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (identity)._

## GW-015

The canonical query is the request target after the first `?`. If there is no `?`, the canonical query is the empty string.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (edge-platform)._

## GW-017

Canonical query ordering sorts parameters by name only. Where a name repeats, the parameters keep the order in which they arrived.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (billing)._

## GW-019

Query parameters are joined `name=value`, pairs separated by `&`. A parameter with no `=` is treated as having an empty value and is still written with a trailing `=`.

_Recorded by K. Mwangi (edge-platform)._

## GW-023

Only the `x-gw-*` header family is signed. Everything else is excluded to keep the signed set small.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (sre-core)._

## GW-025

Header names are lowercased for both the canonical header block and the signed header name list.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (identity)._

## GW-027

The canonical header block writes one header per line as `name:value`, lines joined by LF, sorted by name. There is no trailing LF after the final header line.

_Recorded by P. Oyelaran (edge-platform)._

## GW-029

The signed header name list is the lowercased names in the same sorted order, joined by `;`.

_Recorded by R. Okonkwo (edge-platform)._

## GW-031

Header names are compared and sorted as raw bytes after lowercasing. No locale-aware collation.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (edge-platform)._

## GW-034

The key id travels in the `x-gw-key-id` request header. Its value is matched case-insensitively on the header NAME; the value itself is used verbatim.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (partner-integrations)._

## GW-038

A key id that does not resolve to an approved key file is a hard rejection. The pipeline never falls back to a default key.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (edge-platform)._

## GW-041

Header values are signed exactly as received, byte for byte, including any leading or trailing whitespace.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (partner-integrations)._

## GW-044

Verification compares the presented signature against the recomputed one in constant time.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (fraud-ops)._

## GW-047

The Authorization header format is exactly `GW-HMAC-SHA256 keyId=<id>, signature=<hex>` - one space after the scheme, one comma and one space between the parameters.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (partner-integrations)._

## GW-049

A request carrying an Authorization header is verified. A request without one is signed. There is no explicit mode flag.

_Recorded by P. Oyelaran (partner-integrations)._

## GW-052

The canonical request string is terminated with a trailing newline before the HMAC is computed.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (fraud-ops)._

## GW-055

The pipeline never performs network access. Signing is a pure local computation over the request and the key material.

_Recorded by A. Nakamura (edge-platform)._

## GW-058

Evidence is emitted as newline-delimited JSON: one compact object per input record, in input order, each line terminated by LF including the last.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (identity)._

# 2025-09-30 migration kickoff

Attendees: J. Delacroix, R. Okonkwo, L. Fontaine, D. Achterberg, P. Oyelaran, M. Lindqvist, A. Nakamura, S. Varga

## Ledger smoke test

The identity team want the evidence files kept for 14 days after cutover. Key files are distributed by the provisioning job, which data-plane own. M. Lindqvist asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the ledger dashboard.

## Umbrella sandbox

R. Okonkwo checked that the same disputes request produces the same canonical hash on gw-edge-01 and gw-edge-03. The access log truncates query strings longer than 1024 bytes. The request itself is not truncated. The catalog replay set has 820 requests, of which 27 carry a query string. The batch reader on gw-edge-01 tolerates a trailing newline at the end of the input file. M. Lindqvist asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the payouts dashboard.

## Evidence retention

Disk on gw-edge-02 was at 32 percent after the replay and was cleared by hand. The signer account on gw-edge-04 has no outbound network route, which identity verified again on 2025-09-30. Requests with a body over 512 bytes are rejected upstream of the signer and never reach it.

## Catalog smoke test

S. Varga will rerun the reconciliation replay once Umbrella finish their client release. The webhooks dashboard now splits signature mismatches by key id and by partner. Alert thresholds for settlement stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed.

## Signed header set

D. Achterberg raised that a header outside the signed set can be changed in transit without anyone noticing. Decision for MS-HMAC-SHA256: the `x-ms-*` header family and `content-type` are signed, and nothing else. A. Nakamura will confirm with the partners affected.

## SDK rollout

Header count per request on orders is between 33 and 13 in the sampled traffic. The legacy signer peaked at roughly 20k requests per minute on orders during the last cycle. M. Lindqvist reported that the payouts cutover is on track for the week of 2025-09-30. M. Lindqvist asked whether settlement still needs the old batch window. Nobody objected to dropping it.

## Payouts cutover

The identity team want the evidence files kept for 14 days after cutover. Evidence for refunds is written to the spool directory and collected every 29 minutes. The settlement queue drained in 31 minutes after the replay, which is within the agreed window. The batch reader on gw-edge-04 tolerates a trailing newline at the end of the input file. A. Nakamura checked that the same payouts request produces the same canonical hash on gw-edge-04 and gw-edge-01.

## Rollback rehearsal

Globex use the same key id for disputes and orders. That is allowed. The payments-api team asked that query parameters carrying account numbers be masked in the dashboards. Northwind confirmed they are on SDK 3.1 in production and 3.2 in their sandbox. Capacity headroom on reconciliation is about 50 percent at the current peak. Alert thresholds for ledger stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed.

## Settlement smoke test

The payouts smoke test covers one signed request and one verified request per key id. Requests with a body over 1024 bytes are rejected upstream of the signer and never reach it. Mismatch rate on onboarding was 0.9 percent over the window, all of it from one Umbrella sandbox client.

## Settlement runbook

The webhooks replay set has 3414 requests, of which 12 carry a query string. The identity team want the evidence files kept for 7 days after cutover. The identity team asked for one more dry run on gw-edge-01 before disputes moves.

## Load test

R. Okonkwo reported that the payouts cutover is on track for the week of 2025-09-30. Evidence for settlement is written to the spool directory and collected every 50 minutes. Capacity headroom on onboarding is about 47 percent at the current peak.

## String terminator

D. Achterberg compared the design doc line by line with what the signer hands to HMAC. Agreed: for the export signer, the string to sign ends with a line feed after the last field. The current client release already behaves this way.

## Header values

Northwind reported mismatches on requests whose header values carry runs of spaces. M. Lindqvist proposed, and the room agreed, that for BX-HMAC-SHA256 spaces and tabs are stripped from each end of every header value and the inside of the value is left as it is. The client libraries follow in their next release.

results.content:
Contoso reported mismatches on requests whose header values carry runs of spaces. Agreed: for MS-HMAC-SHA256, spaces and tabs are stripped from each end of every header value and the inside of the value is left as it is. A. Nakamura will update the client notes.

## Load test

The sre-core team want the evidence files kept for 30 days after cutover. Requests with a body over 512 bytes are rejected upstream of the signer and never reach it. The onboarding dashboard now splits signature mismatches by key id and by partner.

## How these notes work

Each session minutes what was agreed, per signer. The register is left as it is. Where minutes turn out to be wrong they are corrected at a later session, in an item that begins "Correction to the minutes of", and the correction is what counts. An item that brings one signer in line with another copies the other's rule as it stood on that day; it does not follow what the other signer does afterwards. An item agreed as effective with a release takes effect on the day that release becomes generally available, and the release calendar has those dates.

## Key loading

Key file handling came up during the rotation rehearsal. Agreed: for the export signer, the key file is used whole, line ending included. T. Bergstrom will update the client notes.

## Header value spacing

Contoso's client pads some header values and the 2 sides end up hashing different bytes. K. Mwangi proposed, and the room agreed, that for the webhook signer header values go into the header block exactly as received, byte for byte. T. Bergstrom will update the client notes.

## Key id matching

P. Oyelaran raised key ids that arrive in the wrong case. M. Lindqvist proposed, and the room agreed, that for the admin signer the key id is matched exactly as sent. T. Bergstrom will update the client notes.

## Payouts replay results

The edge-platform team asked that query parameters carrying account numbers be masked in the dashboards. Latency through the signer stayed under 4ms at p99 across the payouts replay. The key directory on gw-edge-03 is readable by the signer accounts only. The signer account on gw-edge-02 has no outbound network route, which billing verified again on 2025-09-30. J. Delacroix checked that the same webhooks request produces the same canonical hash on gw-edge-01 and gw-edge-04.

## Header values

Globex's client pads some header values and the 2 sides end up hashing different bytes. Decision for the admin signer: header values go into the header block exactly as received, byte for byte. No change for anyone else.

## SDK rollout

Disk on gw-edge-02 was at 38 percent after the replay and was cleared by hand. Header count per request on refunds is between 21 and 17 in the sampled traffic. The rollback rehearsal for onboarding took 32 minutes end to end on gw-edge-01. J. Delacroix has the action to circulate the webhooks numbers before the next session.

## Rollback rehearsal

The reconciliation queue drained in 16 minutes after the replay, which is within the agreed window. Contoso reported 18 failed requests on 2025-09-30, all traced to an expired sandbox credential on their side. Umbrella confirmed they are on SDK 3.1 in production and 3.2 in their sandbox. The ledger dashboard now splits signature mismatches by key id and by partner. The legacy signer peaked at roughly 41k requests per minute on catalog during the last cycle.

## Scope

4 signers besides the one being migrated come up in these sessions, because they share the Perl tree and most of the people. The notes use these names. Inbound request signing, also written as partner request signing, the gateway request scheme or by its identifier GW-HMAC-SHA256, covers requests partners send to the gateway; it is the only one being migrated and the only one the register describes. Outbound webhook signing, also the webhook signer or callback signing, WH-HMAC-SHA256, covers webhook deliveries we send to partners. Export manifest signing, also the export signer or batch manifest signing, BX-HMAC-SHA256, covers the manifest requests of the nightly settlement export. Service mesh signing, also the mesh signer or internal service signing, MS-HMAC-SHA256, covers calls between our own services. Admin API signing, also the admin signer or ops tooling signing, AD-HMAC-SHA256, covers requests from ops tooling to the admin API. A decision minuted for one of them is a decision for that one only.

## Refunds replay results

Disk on gw-edge-04 was at 63 percent after the replay and was cleared by hand. J. Delacroix reported that the catalog cutover is on track for the week of 2025-09-30. The rollback rehearsal for payouts took 26 minutes end to end on gw-edge-03. The payouts dashboard now splits signature mismatches by key id and by partner. Latency through the signer stayed under 7ms at p99 across the payouts replay.

## Evidence retention

The signer account on gw-edge-03 has no outbound network route, which payments-api verified again on 2025-09-30. Initech use the same key id for refunds and orders. That is allowed. The rollback rehearsal for disputes took 50 minutes end to end on gw-edge-04.

## Initech sandbox

Umbrella asked for a second sandbox key id and were pointed at the onboarding form. The legacy signer peaked at roughly 17k requests per minute on ledger during the last cycle. The reconciliation dashboard now splits signature mismatches by key id and by partner. K. Mwangi asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the refunds dashboard.

## Escapes in the target

P. Oyelaran asked whether percent escapes survive the fronting proxy unchanged. Agreed: for callback signing, percent escapes in the path and the query are signed in the case they arrive in. The current client release already behaves this way.

## Ledger runbook

The signer account on gw-edge-03 has no outbound network route, which payments-api verified again on 2025-09-30. Initech use the same key id for refunds and orders. That is allowed. The rollback rehearsal for disputes took 50 minutes end to end on gw-edge-04.

Decision for BX-HMAC-SHA256: query parameters are ordered by name only, and parameters that share a name keep the order they arrived in. Documented in the client notes the same day.
04: Correction to the minutes of 2025-10-07: the item on the query parameter ordering recorded there under MS-HMAC-SHA256 was agreed for admin API signing, not for MS-HMAC-SHA256. Nothing changed for MS-HMAC-SHA256 that day.
04: Ordering of repeated parameters was raised by Globex. Decision for callback signing: query parameters are ordered by name and then by value, with each value percent-decoded before it is compared. J. Delacroix will confirm with the partners affected.
04: 3 client libraries were run against the current ordering and they disagree with each other on requests that repeat a name. Agreed for the admin signer: query parameters are ordered by name and then by value, both compared byte by byte on the text exactly as it appears in the target, with nothing decoded, effective with admin CLI 2.2. Until admin CLI 2.2 is generally available, what is in place now stays.
06: Ordering of repeated parameters was raised by Umbrella. Agreed to bring the query parameter ordering of export manifest signing in line with that of internal service signing, as it stands today.
06: 3 client libraries were run against the current ordering and they disagree with each other on requests that repeat a name. Agreed to bring the query parameter ordering of outbound webhook signing in line with that of partner request signing, as it stands today.
07: 3 client libraries were run against the current ordering and they disagree with each other on requests that repeat a name. Agreed: for callback signing, query parameters are ordered by name and then by value, both compared byte by byte on the text exactly as it appears in the target, with nothing decoded. Effective from this meeting.
07: R. Okonkwo traced a batch of failures to the order of repeated query parameters. Decision for internal service signing: query parameters are ordered by name and then by value, with each value percent-decoded before it is compared. No change for anyone else.
08: 3 client libraries were run against the current ordering and they disagree with each other on requests that repeat a name. Agreed to bring the query parameter ordering of the gateway request scheme in line with that of batch manifest signing, as it stands today.
10: M. Lindqvist traced a batch of failures to the order of repeated query parameters. Agreed: for batch manifest signing, query parameters are ordered by name and then by value, with each value percent-decoded before it is compared. Documented in the client notes the same day.
12: 3 client libraries were run against the current ordering and they disagree with each other on requests that repeat a name. Umbrella asked for a change so that, for partner request signing, query parameters are ordered by name and then by value, with each value percent-decoded before it is compared. Declined. The cost of changing every client is not worth it.

03: Umbrella's client pads some header values and the 2 sides end up hashing different bytes. Agreed: for the admin signer, spaces and tabs are stripped from each end of every header value and every run of spaces and tabs inside it is collapsed to a single space. No change for anyone else.
03: M. Lindqvist found 2 code paths that read the key file differently. Decision for export manifest signing: the key file is used whole, line ending included. Documented in the client notes the same day.
03: Umbrella's client pads some header values and the 2 sides end up hashing different bytes. For batch manifest signing, as a trial: spaces and tabs are stripped from each end of every header value and every run of spaces and tabs inside it is collapsed to a single space. To be confirmed or backed out at the next session but one.
03: The rotation rehearsal turned up a key file written with a different line ending. Decision for outbound webhook signing: the line ending is stripped from the key file before the key is used. Northwind have been told.
04: Correction to the minutes of 2025-10-07: the item on the loading of the key file recorded there under callback signing was agreed for service mesh signing, not for callback signing. Nothing changed for callback signing that day.
04: Correction to the minutes of 2025-10-07: the item on the treatment of header values recorded there under admin API signing was agreed for service mesh signing, not for admin API signing. Nothing changed for admin API signing that day.
04: Globex's client pads some header values and the 2 sides end up hashing different bytes. Decision for inbound request signing: spaces and tabs are stripped from each end of every header value and the inside of the value is left as it is. Globex have been told.
04: Umbrella's integration upper-cases every header value it controls, key ids included. Agreed to bring the key id matching of the admin signer in line with that of service mesh signing, as it stands today.
04: D. Achterberg asked whether a key id is compared as text or folded first. P. Oyelaran proposed that for the export signer the key id is matched without regard to case. Parked until there are numbers to look at; nothing changes for now.
05: Header value spacing came up again from Northwind. For the admin signer, as a trial: header values are stripped and collapsed and then lowercased. To be confirmed or backed out at the next session but one.
05: Correction to the minutes of 2025-10-07: the item on the loading of the key file recorded there under batch manifest signing was agreed for the webhook signer, not for batch manifest signing. Nothing changed for batch manifest signing that day.
05: Correction to the minutes of 2025-10-14: the item on the loading of the key file recorded there under MS-HMAC-SHA256 was agreed for the admin signer, not for MS-HMAC-SHA256. Nothing changed for MS-HMAC-SHA256 that day.
05: Contoso asked whether a line ending in a key file matters. For the mesh signer, as a trial: the key file is used whole, line ending included. To be confirmed or backed out at the next session but one.
06: Umbrella's requests are rejected as unknown because their key ids arrive in upper case. Agreed: for AD-HMAC-SHA256, the key id is matched without regard to case. The current client release already behaves this way.
06: For batch manifest signing, the trial started on 2025-10-07 is backed out. The cost of changing every client is not worth it. From now spaces and tabs are stripped from each end of every header value and the inside of the value is left as it is, as before the trial.
06: Key file handling came up during the rotation rehearsal. Agreed to bring the loading of the key file of AD-HMAC-SHA256 in line with that of the export signer, as it stands today.
06: For export manifest signing, the proposal of 2025-10-14 that the key id is matched without regard to case was withdrawn. It made things worse in the partner test. What was in place before stays.
06: Case of key ids came up from Initech. Northwind asked that for internal service signing the key id is matched exactly as sent. Not adopted. It came too late for this cutover.
07: Contoso's integration upper-cases every header value it controls, key ids included. Umbrella asked for a change so that, for callback signing, the key id is matched exactly as sent. Declined. The numbers did not support it.
07: A. Nakamura reran the comparison between what clients send and what arrives. Any value a client wraps or pads comes out of the fronting proxy with different spacing inside as well as at the ends. Agreed: for callback signing, spaces and tabs are stripped from each end of every header value and every run of spaces and tabs inside it is collapsed to a single space. D. Achterberg will update the client notes.
07: For ops tooling signing, the trial started on 2025-10-21 is backed out. It changes values that are case sensitive. From now header values go into the header block exactly as received, byte for byte, as before the trial.
08: For service mesh signing, the trial started on 2025-10-21 is confirmed: the key file is used whole, line ending included.
08: Correction to the minutes of 2025-11-04: the item on the treatment of header values recorded there under outbound webhook signing was agreed for GW-HMAC-SHA256, not for outbound webhook signing. Nothing changed for outbound webhook signing that day.
10: Globex's requests are rejected as unknown because their key ids arrive in upper case. Northwind asked for a change so that, for inbound request signing, the key id is matched without regard to case. Declined. It would break integrations already in the field.
10: Header value spacing came up again from Initech. Globex asked for a change so that, for inbound request signing, header values are stripped and collapsed and then lowercased. Declined. Sharing that code saves a dozen lines and changes every signature.

# Appendix - Release Calendar

General availability dates for the client libraries and components the signers depend on. A change minuted as effective with a release takes effect on that release's date.

## Host gw-edge-04

Latency through the signer stayed under 5ms at p99 across the disputes replay. The partner-integrations team want the evidence files kept for 30 days after cutover. M. Lindqvist reported that the webhooks cutover is on track for the week of 2025-12-02. Alert thresholds for webhooks stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed.

## Host gw-edge-03

Contoso reported 37 failed requests on 2025-10-07, all traced to an expired sandbox credential on their side. T. Bergstrom checked that the same refunds request produces the same canonical hash on gw-edge-01 and gw-edge-03. The access log truncates query strings longer than 2048 bytes. The request itself is not truncated. The edge-platform team want the evidence files kept for 14 days after cutover. A Umbrella engineer joined for this item and dropped off afterwards.

## Evidence retention

P. Oyelaran reported that the catalog cutover is on track for the week of 2025-12-02. The partner-integrations team asked that query parameters carrying account numbers be masked in the dashboards. Header count per request on ledger is between 5 and 10 in the sampled traffic. Evidence for payouts is written to the spool directory and collected every 29 minutes.

## Load test

Alert thresholds for reconciliation stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed. Key files are distributed by the provisioning job, which data-plane own. S. Varga asked whether disputes still needs the old batch window. Nobody objected to dropping it. The catalog queue drained in 54 minutes after the replay, which is within the agreed window.

- receiver kit 2.0: general availability 2025-11-28.

- admin CLI 2.2: general availability 2026-02-03.

- export client 1.4: general availability 2025-12-18.

## Umbrella update

M. Lindqvist asked whether onboarding still needs the old batch window. Nobody objected to dropping it. Key files are distributed by the provisioning job, which data-plane own. T. Bergstrom reported that the webhooks cutover is on track for the week of 2025-11-18. The key directory on gw-edge-03 is readable by the signer accounts only. J. Delacroix asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the webhooks dashboard.

- SDK 3.3: general availability 2026-01-13.

## SDK rollout

Header count per request on settlement is between 21 and 14 in the sampled traffic. A Contoso engineer joined for this item and dropped off afterwards. The batch reader on gw-edge-02 tolerates a trailing newline at the end of the input file.

## Access and accounts

Umbrella use the same key id for ledger and orders. That is allowed. The edge-platform team want the evidence files kept for 14 days after cutover. R. Okonkwo raised that the catalog runbook still names the Perl script. To be fixed after cutover. The legacy signer peaked at roughly 27k requests per minute on disputes during the last cycle. The batch reader on gw-edge-02 tolerates a trailing newline at the end of the input file.

## Access and accounts

Disk on gw-edge-03 was at 73 percent after the replay and was cleared by hand. Evidence for reconciliation is written to the spool directory and collected every 6 minutes. The rollback rehearsal for ledger took 17 minutes end to end on gw-edge-02.

- SDK 3.2: general availability 2025-11-03.

## Host gw-edge-03

The key directory on gw-edge-03 is readable by the signer accounts only. The access log truncates query strings longer than 512 bytes. The request itself is not truncated. The legacy signer peaked at roughly 32k requests per minute on onboarding during the last cycle.

## Settlement cutover

The key directory on gw-edge-03 is readable by the signer accounts only. The access log truncates query strings longer than 1024 bytes. The request itself is not truncated. Alert thresholds for payouts stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed. Capacity headroom on payouts is about 69 percent at the current peak.

## Payouts smoke test

L. Fontaine checked that the same settlement request produces the same canonical hash on gw-edge-01 and gw-edge-02. J. Delacroix will rerun the webhooks replay once Northwind finish their client release. The refunds queue drained in 30 minutes after the replay, which is within the agreed window.

## Settlement cutover

The disputes replay set has 594 requests, of which 27 carry a query string. The batch reader on gw-edge-04 tolerates a trailing newline at the end of the input file. Mismatch rate on disputes was 0.1 percent over the window, all of it from one Globex sandbox client.

- mesh sidecar 0.9: general availability 2025-11-20.

## Settlement cutover

A. Nakamura raised that the orders runbook still names the Perl script. To be fixed after cutover. The rollback rehearsal for orders took 29 minutes end to end on gw-edge-03. Mismatch rate on onboarding was 0.2 percent over the window, all of it from one Globex sandbox client.

## Host gw-edge-03

Latency through the signer stayed under 8ms at p99 across the refunds replay. Capacity headroom on onboarding is about 28 percent at the current peak. The signer account on gw-edge-02 has no outbound network route, which partner-integrations verified again on 2025-11-18. Requests with a body over 512 bytes are rejected upstream of the signer and never reach it. The fraud-ops team want the evidence files kept for 90 days after cutover.

## SDK rollout

steps.message:
I finished the port. `/app/src/pipeline.ts` now builds with `tsc -p /app/tsconfig.json` and runs as `node /app/dist/pipeline.js`. Its output for the sample is in `/app/out/evidence.ndjson`, and two runs give identical bytes.

**What the sample shows**
- Record 6 carries a real signature dated 2025-12-08, and it now **verifies**. That checks the rules below as a set, including the key handling and the missing trailing newline.
- Record 7 is dated 2025-11-20 and is rejected as `signature-mismatch`. I checked that its signature is only reproducible under the pre-freeze rules (trailing newline, `UNSIGNED` for empty bodies), so that rejection is expected.
- Record 4 names `gw-prod-03` and is `unknown-key-id`. Record 5 has no key id and is `missing-key-id`.

**Why the old port failed**
The decision register is only the starting point. Later session notes reversed or changed several of its rules. The ones that apply to GW-HMAC-SHA256 at the 2025-12-09 rollout:
- **String to sign:** no trailing newline (12-02 scheme freeze). The register's GW-052 said to add one.
- **Body hash:** always the SHA-256 of the body, including for an empty body (11-25). The register's `UNSIGNED` token is gone. SDK 3.2.1 went generally available on 12-01, so this was already in force.
- **Header values:** spaces and tabs are stripped from both ends, and runs inside a value collapse to one space (10-14, plus the 11-04 item that 11-11 corrected to GW).
- **Signed headers:** every header except `authorization`, with names lowercased and sorted bytewise. All 5 partners signed off by 12-04, ahead of the 12-05 deadline.
- **Unchanged from the register:**
  - Names are joined with `;` (the `,` proposal was withdrawn, and the 11-25 `,` item was corrected to another signer).
  - Valueless query parameters get a trailing `=`.
  - Query parameters sort by name only, in arrival order.
  - The key id is matched exactly as sent.
- **Not applied:**
  - Dot-segment collapsing waits for SDK 3.3, which only goes generally available on 2026-01-13.
  - Percent-escape uppercasing needed proxy captures showing rewriting, and the captures show escapes pass through unchanged.

**Keys**
- **Roster:** the active roster is `gw-prod-01` and `gw-prod-02`. The legacy strace and lsof show only those two being opened. `gw-prod-03` belongs to the export signer, and the 24-key-rotation-runbook and 12-2025-12-09-rollout notes put inbound signing's move to it in a later Q1 window.
- **Line ending:** the trailing line ending is stripped from the key file. The notes don't state this for GW. I inferred it because record 6 only verifies with the stripped key.

**Network**
The webhook strace shows a socket connect and the legacy strace shows none, so signing is pure local computation. The sources contain no network client and no `http` or `net` imports.

The code hardcodes the roster as those two ids, so a new key would need a code change.
